$comment: Bylines shown under the Hamlet wordmark, one picked at random each launch.
The point is joy: ham radio is intimidating, and a small daily chuckle costs
nothing and softens the whole thing. Shakespeare is public domain (the man
died in 1616), so these are free to use and to alter.
'source' names the play the line is bent from, so the joke is legible even to
someone who doesn't know the original. Keep the list long enough that a
regular user rarely sees a repeat, and never show the same one twice in a row.

bylines.text: To key or not to key — that is the question
The band's the thing
Alas, poor Yagi — I knew him well
Something is rotten in the state of my SWR
There are more things in heaven and earth than are dreamt of in your bandplan
Brevity is the soul of wit, and of CW
Get thee to a repeater
Though this be madness, yet there is method in the mode
The rest is silence — or possibly a dead battery
Once more unto the band, dear friends, once more
We few, we happy few, we band of operators
Uneasy lies the head that wears a headset
Cry havoc, and let slip the dogs of DX
Friends, Romans, countrymen — lend me your ears, I'm calling CQ
Beware the ides of QRM
The static is not in our stars, but in ourselves
All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely operators
The course of true DX never did run smooth
Lord, what fools these mortals be — they never worked ten meters
The lunatic, the lover and the poet are of imagination all compact — the ham checks the solar flux first
What's in a name? That which we call a callsign
Parting is such sweet sorrow — 73
But soft, what light through yonder window breaks? It's the S-meter
A plague o' both your houses — and your neighbor's plasma TV
Some are born to DX, some achieve DX, and some have DX thrust upon them
If music be the food of love, play on — forty meters, after dark
Now is the winter of our discontent made glorious summer by this son of a beacon
A signal, a signal — my kingdom for a signal
Double, double, toil and trouble — dipole burn and antenna bubble
Is this a dagger which I see before me? No — it's the whip antenna
Out, out, brief candle — and check the fuse while you're up
Full fathom five thy antenna lies
We are such stuff as dreams are made on, and mostly copper wire
O brave new world, that has such operators in it
Hell is empty and all the QRM is here
Exit, pursued by a beam
All that glisters is not gold-plated
The lady doth protest too much — she's over-modulating
Shall I compare thee to a summer's band?
Love is not love which alters when it alteration finds — unlike the ionosphere
Cowards die many times before their deaths; the valiant call CQ but once
Nothing will come of nothing — speak again, you're breaking up
How sharper than a serpent's tooth it is to have a thankless coax
The better part of valor is discretion — and a good ground rod
Screw your courage to the sticking place, and key up
